about.title: Rialto Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Rialto sits where several busy routes converge. Riverside Avenue carries traffic north toward the 210, Baseline Road and Foothill Boulevard cross the heart of town, and SR-210 moves freeway volume along the city's north edge. In 2025, public records show 432 injury collisions in Rialto, 637 people hurt, and 10 traffic deaths. Those reports cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., when the workweek is ending and roads are full. If one of those crashes involved you, the days afterward can feel disorienting: medical visits, a car that may not run, and an adjuster calling before you've had time to think. LawProactive is here to take one item off that list. We are a free connection service, not a law firm. Tell us what happened, and we'll match you with an independent California attorney who handles Rialto car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Rialto Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock is already running
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but claims involving a city, county, or state vehicle or roadway can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney in our network can pin down which deadline applies to your Rialto crash before it slips by.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame; your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage. The attorney you're connected with will push back if the other insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: No fee unless there's a recovery
items.desc: Every attorney in the LawProactive network works on contingency, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost quality of life in a standard car accident case. Our connection service costs you nothing, either.

items.question: I was hit on Riverside Avenue by a driver in a city or county vehicle. Does that change anything?
items.answer: Yes, it can matter a great deal. When a government entity such as the City of Rialto or San Bernardino County is involved, California generally requires a formal claim within six months, far shorter than the usual two-year window. Missing that step can end the case before it starts, so it's worth speaking with an attorney quickly to confirm who owned the vehicle and what deadline applies.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: We'd encourage you to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to shrink or deny your claim later, and you are not required to give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer. Instead, focus on gathering what you can: photos of the vehicles, the intersection, your injuries, and contact information for any witnesses.

items.question: I think I may have been partly at fault for the crash on Baseline Road. Can I still make a claim?
items.answer: In most cases, yes. California follows pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility rather than eliminated. If you were found 25 percent at fault, for example, you could still pursue the remaining 75 percent of your damages. An attorney can review the police report and evidence to make sure fault is assigned fairly.
